generator.note: Every dimension below is a module constant in that script or a measurement of the shipped STEP. --check rebuilds from those constants and compares topology and volume-level facts; it never compares bytes, because the STEP header carries a write timestamp.

description: Suspension wishbone / A-arm. Two coaxial chassis-side bushing eyes on the y pivot axis fork through two swept arms with opposite out-of-plane profiles, tied by one swept cross-brace, into a single upright-side ball-joint boss. Frame: +x outboard toward the upright, +y the chassis pivot axis (fore-aft), +z up. SI metres.

dimensions_m.measurement: tight bounding box via BRepBndLib::AddOptimal and BRepGProp volume of tests/fixtures/parts/wishbone.step after reopening it; OpenCASCADE's default 1e-7 m box gap has been removed from each bound.

wall_thickness.method: inward ray cast along the area-weighted vertex normal against the full tessellation of the reopened STEP
wall_thickness.thinnest_location: the bushing annulus at both eyes: eye_outer 0.030 - bore 0.008 = 0.022 m
wall_thickness.why_it_is_a_first_class_dimension: the mesher snaps boundary nodes to the exact BRep inside a band of 1.5 * fill_h, so a wall thinner than that band lets both sides snap onto each other and the skin goes non-manifold. An earlier 24/9.5 mm eye and 28/12 mm boss left a 14.5 mm minimum wall and failed the product fill guard at h = 8 mm and h = 16 mm.

fixtures.label: support_y_lo
fixtures.description: Bonded rigid-pin idealisation on the internal bushing bore; all translational DOFs constrained on the actual chassis interface.

fixtures.label: support_y_hi
fixtures.description: Second bonded rigid-pin idealisation. The separated internal bores create the chassis pivot baseline and torsional load path.

load.label: loaded_ball_joint_bore
load.resultant_direction_note: 32.005 degrees from vertical, tilted inboard (-x). Vertical plus lateral, no invented fore-aft component.

derivation.basis: rounded 4.717 kN combined bump/cornering design load
derivation.purpose: Produces a distributed bending-plus-torsion field between the chassis pin bores and ball-joint bore in the declared linear-elastic model.
derivation.status: authored numerical design load, explicitly not a measured vehicle event

hand_check.linearity: The solver is linear elastostatic: scaling the conserved resultant scales stress and displacement by the same factor while leaving the ZZ relative indicator unchanged.
hand_check.status: The published bore-loaded take records 202.486 MPa peak stress and 1.19836 mm peak displacement in manifest.json.

load.description: The conserved resultant is distributed over the complete internal ball-joint bore, where the upright joint actually transfers load. Both chassis constraints likewise act on internal bushing bores; no exterior housing face is treated as ground.

mesh.h_rationale: 0.0055 m keeps the 1.5 * fill_h snap band at 0.00825 m, 2.67x below the measured 0.02207 m minimum wall. Geometry and support/load grading are disabled for the uniform fill; exact bore regions drive boundary conditions.

boundary_node_supply_at_h.purpose: distributed internal interfaces rather than point or edge constraints

mesh.status: Wall-resolving tet verification solve with distributed bore interfaces. The cinema's tet10 card teaches the supported higher-order element explicitly; the manifest records the executed solve order.

region_selection.method: The GUI grows region ids by flood-filling the display tessellation across shared edges while adjacent facet normals stay within 30 degrees (src/pipeline/src/scene.cpp Model::load), over the per-face triangle soup built in TopExp face order. Region id therefore does not equal CAD face index. The map below comes from a fresh built-GUI overlay capture of every region 0..10 rather than from CAD ordering assumptions.
region_selection.verification: A fresh GUI face-overlay sweep captured all regions 0..10 from the built product. The cinema uses fix 9; fix 10; loadface 5.
region_selection.area_keys: Ball-joint bore analytic area 0.00376991118 m2; each bushing bore 0.00241274316 m2.
region_selection.why_the_interfaces_survive: Each selected bore is one uninterrupted cylindrical region bounded by annular edges. The applied regions are the three visible internal bores, not adjacent arms or exterior housings.
region_selection.surface_quality: Worst convex edge 77.98 degrees, worst re-entrant crotch 290.44 degrees, measured over every tessellated edge. No knife edge, no tangential cusp, and no non-adjacent CAD face pair in contact, so there is no coincident-skin site anywhere on the part.

checks_enforced_by_generator: valid BRep, exactly one solid, positive volume, before and after the bores are cut
all three bore axes classify OUT along their whole sleeve length, and wall material classifies IN just outside each bore
exactly three cylindrical faces at the two bore radii, each at full sleeve area, so no bore was interrupted by a boolean
both arms exceed 0.012 m of out-of-plane excursion from the plane through the three eye centres, with opposite signs, so the fork is never coplanar
each arm spine travels at least 0.015 m in z

measured_out_of_plane_m.note: Signed peak distance from the plane through the two eye centres and the boss centre. Opposite signs are the numeric statement that this is a three-dimensional fork and not a perforated plate. The spines are unchanged from the first revision; only member and ring radii moved.
